uncertainty_notes: 1. THE RESEARCH BRIEF IS HALF WRONG ABOUT THE ENGLISH PAGE, AND THE CORRECTION IS GOOD NEWS. The brief states this curriculum has NO dedicated English page and is documented only by an Italian note. CORRECT: the ORIENTATION PORTAL page exists only in Italian - verified by fetching both ?lang=en and the /corsidistudioen/ path, which return the identical Italian document byte for byte, whereas the same patterns serve genuine English fact-sheets for Federico II's fully-English degrees - and on it the curriculum receives exactly one sentence. INCORRECT: a dedicated English page DOES exist at https://www.iat.unina.it/environmental-sustainability/ on the degree programme's own official site, and an official English study plan exists at https://www.iat.unina.it/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Annex_1_EN_LM_IAT_25-26.pdf . Much of this record is therefore sourced from official ENGLISH unina.it documents. 2. THE WORST NAMING TRAP: TWO CURRICULA SHARE ONE NAME. 'Sostenibilita Ambientale' (Italian-taught) and 'Environmental Sustainability' (English-taught) are literal translations of each other but are FORMALLY SEPARATE CURRICULA with separate course tables. The binding 2026/2027 study plan does not use the English name at all - it heads the two tables 'Curriculum Sostenibilita Ambientale in Italiano' and 'Curriculum Sostenibilita Ambientale in Inglese'. The Manifesto uses 'Environmental Sustainability'. The website uses '``Environmental Sustainability`` curriculum in English'. ANY REQUEST MUST SAY 'IN ENGLISH' / 'IN INGLESE' EXPLICITLY, or the applicant may be enrolled on the Italian twin. 3. THE DIPLOMA CARRIES THE ITALIAN DEGREE NAME ONLY. The qualification is 'Laurea Magistrale in Ingegneria per l'Ambiente e il Territorio' (official English rendering per Art. 1: 'Environmental and Territorial Engineering'), class LM-35. The curriculum is a study-plan choice and does not appear in the legal name - exactly as the brief anticipated. Note the partner-facing English name varies even inside unina.it: 'Environmental and Territorial Engineering' (Art. 1, Annex 1, double-degree page) vs 'Environmental and Territory Engineering' (DICEA placement-test page). 4. THE CURRICULUM IS CHOSEN AFTER ENROLMENT, AND NOTHING GUARANTEES IT RUNS. There is no separate application, no seat allocation and no admission route for the English path; a student enrols in the LM-35 degree and declares the curriculum in the Study Plan. No minimum cohort, no activation rule and no enrolment figures for the English path are published anywhere. This is the same structural risk found across Federico II's curriculum-level English offerings. 5. THE 18 FREE-CHOICE CFU ARE THE BIGGEST THREAT TO THE 'FULLY ENGLISH' CLAIM. 15% of the degree sits in a free-choice slot that, unlike at some sister degrees, is NOT restricted to English-taught courses; Art. 9 opens it to any course in the whole University subject to a coherence check by the Coordination Committee, and the Manifesto's recommended lists are drawn from the Italian curricula. Nothing published guarantees that 18 CFU of suitable English electives exist. Verify with the Coordinator before committing. 6. B2 ENGLISH IS A REAL ADMISSION REQUIREMENT HERE - DO NOT GENERALISE FROM OTHER FEDERICO II ENGINEERING DEGREES, several of which set only a B1 Italian-OR-English gate and treat B2 English as a graduation matter. This degree requires B2 English in Art. 4, in Art. 5 and on the central record, proved by "attestato rilasciato da un organismo competente". BUT: no list of accepted certificates and no score thresholds are published; 'organismo competente' is undefined; and no waiver is published for graduates of English-medium universities (a waiver that IS explicit at sister degrees). 7. THE CONDITIONAL-ENROLMENT CONCESSION IS PUBLISHED IN ONLY ONE PLACE. The right to enrol 'sub-condizione' without B2, provided a certificate is obtained by the first semester of year 2, appears on the orientation portal but NOT in the binding Didactic Regulations, which state the requirement flatly. The two are not reconciled, and it is unclear whether the student office extends the concession to holders of foreign qualifications. 8. THE ADMISSION INTERVIEW HAS NO PUBLISHED PROCEDURE AT ALL - and for an overseas applicant this is the largest operational unknown. No panel, no dates, no booking method, no remote-sitting statement, no turnaround, no written decision, and - critically - no statement of the language in which it is conducted for a candidate applying to the English curriculum. Nor is it stated how the 24/30 exemption is computed from a foreign transcript with no Italian 30-point average. Anyone below 24/30, or on a non-Italian grading scale, must raise this with the Coordinator early. 9. THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS ARE UNUSUALLY RIGID AND PUBLISH NO ESCAPE CLAUSE. The three-level SSD table demands at least 96 CFU of specified content and hard minimums in Idraulica (ICAR/01), Geotecnica (ICAR/07) and Scienza delle Costruzioni (ICAR/08) - civil-engineering staples absent from most environmental-science, chemistry, geology and mechanical bachelors. Unlike several sister degrees, Arts. 4-5 contain NO clause empowering the committee to recognise content-equivalent credits from other SSDs and NO 'alignment path' for partially-qualified candidates. Whether such discretion is exercised in practice is not published. Nor is it stated how foreign ECTS map to Italian SSD codes, whether a 180-ECTS three-year bachelor is required, or what syllabus evidence is accepted. 10. THE CENTRAL UNINA.IT RECORD IS STALE ON TWO POINTS. It publishes a curricular table that adds 'INF/07 = min 9' - a requirement absent from the current Regulations - and omits the new post-reform SSD codes. It also names 'Coordinatore: Prof. Francesco PIROZZI', who is the DEPARTMENT Director, not the programme coordinator. Prefer the Didactic Regulations and the orientation portal. 11. THE COORDINATOR'S NAME IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS FOUR UNINA.IT SOURCES. Current and correct: PROF. ALESSANDRA CESARO (alessandra.cesaro@unina.it, 0817683445) - named as 'Coordinatrice Didattica' on the orientation portal and as 'Coordinatrice del Corso di studio' in a programme news item of 3 July 2026. Stale: Prof. Francesco Pirozzi (central record), Prof. Massimiliano Fabbricino (2024/2025 double-degree decrees and the International Course Catalogue), and 'Prof. Massimiliano Fabbrocino' with the e-mail massimiliano.fabbrocino@unina.it and a telephone number copied from an unrelated Law entry (Catalogue, Kyungpook row - a plain data-entry error). 12. THE DEGREE IS INVISIBLE IN THE UNIVERSITY'S OWN ENGLISH COURSE CATALOGUE. https://www.international.unina.it/international-courses-catalogue/ lists Federico II's English and ITA/ENG master's degrees; neither 'Environmental and Territorial Engineering' nor 'Ingegneria per l'Ambiente e il Territorio' nor 'Environmental Sustainability' appears among them. The degree surfaces only under 'Double degrees'. An international applicant browsing the official English catalogue will therefore never find this curriculum - it is discoverable only through the Italian orientation page or by landing directly on iat.unina.it. This is a discoverability failure, not a sign that the curriculum does not exist. 13. THE SOFIA DOUBLE DEGREE IS TIED TO A CURRICULUM, AND THE SOURCES DISAGREE ON WHICH ONE. The orientation portal restricts it to students "che seguono il Curriculum di Sostenibilita Ambientale" and the programme site's Italian text to "allievi iscritti al PERCORSO TRADIZIONALE (curriculum Sostenibilita Ambientale)" - the traditional, i.e. ITALIAN, path. But the same page's ENGLISH text drops the restriction for Sofia and, for Kyungpook, renders it as "(Master Degree, ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY CURRICULUM)". SO IT IS GENUINELY UNCLEAR WHETHER A STUDENT ON THE ENGLISH CURRICULUM IS ELIGIBLE FOR THE SOFIA DOUBLE DEGREE THE BRIEF ASKS ABOUT. Given that the Sofia partner degree is taught in English and the Catalogue marks the pairing 'ITA/ENG', eligibility is plausible - but it is NOT established by any source. Ask Prof. Cesaro or Prof. Pagliara (francesca.pagliara@unina.it) directly. 14. THE DOUBLE-DEGREE STRUCTURE IS DESCRIBED DIFFERENTLY BY THE WEBSITE AND BY THE RECTORAL DECREE. The website says Sofia participants "frequentare il TERZO SEMESTRE all'Universita di Sofia"; Art. 3 of the decree says the FIRST YEAR is spent at the home university and "nel SECONDO ANNO gli studenti si trasferiscono presso l'Universita partner". For Kyungpook the website says the third AND fourth semesters. The decree is the binding text. 15. A THIRD DOUBLE DEGREE EXISTS IN LAW BUT NOT ON THE WEBSITE. Art. 1.4 of the Regulations and the International Catalogue both record a Double Degree with the Czech University of Life Sciences, Prague, in 'Land and Environmental Engineering' (Catalogue: 'LANGUAGE: ENG'). The programme's own double-degree page lists only Sofia and Kyungpook. Its current status is unclear. 16. THE 2026/2027 'STUDY PLAN' IS THE 2025/2026 DOCUMENT. The file the orientation portal labels 'Piano di studi 2026/2027' is byte-for-byte identical to the one labelled 'Piano di studi 2025/2026' apart from one whitespace character, and its own cover reads "Regolamento proposto in vigore a partire dall'a.a. 2025-2026". No full 2026-2027 Regolamento Didattico had been published as of 30 August 2026 - only a 2026/27 Manifesto degli Studi. The course content is therefore stable across the two years, and the admission articles quoted here are from the 2025-2026 text, reproduced verbatim on the orientation portal page headed 'Aggiornata a.a. 2026/2027'. Re-check when the 2026-2027 regulations appear. 17. A MINOR SSD DISCREPANCY BETWEEN THE ENGLISH AND ITALIAN STUDY PLANS. 'Safety in Chemical Processes' is coded ING-IND/11 (IIND-07/B) in the English Annex 1 but ING-IND/27 (ICHI-02/B) in the Italian Allegato 1 and in the 2026/27 Manifesto. The Italian documents agree with each other and with the course's subject matter; the English annex appears to carry a copy-paste error from the row above. Course title, credits and TAF are identical in both. Similarly 'Environmental Hydraulics' is CER-01/A in the study plan and CEAR-01/A in the Manifesto ('CER' is a truncation of 'CEAR'). 18. TWO DIFFERENT ENROLMENT END DATES, AND TWO DIFFERENT REGIONAL-TAX FIGURES. The binding 'Guida all'iscrizione 2026-27' gives 2 November 2026 as the ordinary matriculation deadline; the programme page gives a year-generic '1 September to 31 October'. Treat 31 October 2026 as safe. On fees, international.unina.it publishes a flat 140 EUR regional tax while the Guida publishes bands of 130/151/173 EUR under D.M. n. 176 of 24 February 2026, with 151 EUR assigned by rule to students whose household resides abroad. Use the Guida. 19. THE NON-EU DEADLINE FOR THE CURRENT CYCLE HAS PASSED. 15 June 2026 was the Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline for a.y. 2026/2027 and, the course being open access, it did not reopen. As of 30 August 2026 a non-EU applicant residing abroad is targeting a.y. 2027/2028, whose deadlines were not yet published. Note also that the second-semester entry point permitted by Art. 5 has no published non-EU pathway. 20. THE 2027/2028 DOUBLE-DEGREE CALLS WERE ANNOUNCED ON 3 JULY 2026 AS 'ABOUT TO BE PUBLISHED' but had not appeared at the expected unina.it document URLs as of 30 August 2026. On the previous years' pattern expect an application deadline around 30 November 2026 and a matriculation deadline around 31 December 2026. 21. THE ENGLISH PLACEMENT TEST INFORMATION IS PARTLY DATED. The DICEA calendar page confirms the test's purpose, scope (eleven engineering master's degrees including this one), online delivery, the esol.unina.it booking route and the 30-hour CLA remedial course, but its published sitting dates belong to earlier cycles; the most recent sitting located was 6 March 2026 (CLA, Via Mezzocannone 8, 4th floor, 50 places, registration 20 February - 1 March 2026). No 2026/27 calendar was published as of the research date. 22. NO CONTACT PERSON FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS DEGREE, unlike several sister engineering master's degrees which name dedicated foreign-enrolment referents. Everything international routes through the Coordinator, the Erasmus referent, or the generic Engineering student office (segreing@unina.it). 23. NO SEAT NUMBERS OF ANY KIND ARE PUBLISHED FOR THE DEGREE - not a total cap, not a non-EU quota, not a cohort size, not an English-curriculum enrolment figure. The absence of a cap is INFERRED from the degree's absence from the 2026/2027 numero-programmato index and from the 'Verifica di preparazione' admission label, not from an explicit statement. The only published cap in this record is the 3 places per double-degree call. 24. TECHNICAL NOTES FOR ANYONE RE-VERIFYING THIS RECORD. (a) www.orientamento.unina.it serves an incomplete TLS certificate chain and is rejected by strict automated fetchers; the pages load normally in a browser. The substantive content and the PDFs verified for this record are consistent with the University-hosted documents on unina.it and orientamento.unina.it, but treat iat.unina.it with appropriate care and prefer the unina.it-hosted copies where both exist. (c) All data in this record was taken from unina.it, orientamento.unina.it, international.unina.it, iat.unina.it and dicea.unina.it only, per the brief.
